title: Content & Growth Marketer
description: About Tradeaze Tradeaze is on-demand delivery for the built environment. Builders' merchants book a delivery in our app, and a vetted driver collects from the branch and delivers to site the same day. We work with national groups like Jewson, Travis Perkins, EH Smith and Lords, and we are growing fast. You would be the second person in growth and marketing, joining as the new brand and website go live. The role You are a content-leaning generalist marketer who uses AI to do the work of a bigger team. Your job is to bring new branches onto Tradeaze and turn them into regular customers. You make the message; we run the system behind it. What you will do Make content for two audiences: the people who use Tradeaze every day (branch staff and drivers), and the people who follow us on LinkedIn as a tech-forward start-up. Posts, short video, case studies, printed pieces, content from around the office Turn one real delivery into three things in a week: a case study, a post and a one-pager sales can carry into a branch Write the campaigns that turn a new branch into a regular customer, from the idea to the words to the design Sit with the marketing team at a merchant head office and run a joint campaign across their branches Keep socials and the blog moving, with AI doing the first draft and you deciding what's good Be out at yards and branches with a camera, and at trade events with a stand Who you are Around 3 years in marketing, in a small team or start-up where you made the work yourself. Less is fine if your work shows it You take ownership. You spot what needs doing and do it without being asked, and you treat the results as yours. You've designed things people actually used: a post, a flyer, a deck. Use whatever tool you like (Figma, Adobe), as long as the work looks professional You write for an audience, whether you write it yourself or set the lines and guidelines and have AI draft it. Either way you know what a counter manager will read and what a LinkedIn follower will stop for You already use AI in your work. You can show us something you shipped with it and talk us through how you use it You've taken a campaign from the idea to launch: the message, the words and the design You come to a conversation with ideas and you enjoy bouncing them off someone You're personable: comfortable with sales reps, a room full of branch managers, and sitting with a merchant head office's marketing team to run a joint campaign You'd rather get it live this week and improve it than plan it for a month Nice to have: paid ads (you've run paid social or search with a budget), events (you've helped run a trade show stand) and email copy (you've written emails that get people to take one clear action) Not for you if: You want a brief handed to you You need an agency to make things You'd rather plan than ship How we work You will report to our GTM Engineer, and you both report to Jack, our CEO. You will work with the GTM Engineer day to day. They own the systems: the CRM, the email platform, the data and the sends. You own the message and the content. You will plan together, brainstorm together, and look at the numbers together every Monday. Jack opens the door with merchant head offices; you and the GTM Engineer run what happens next. You will see your work on a live dashboard: what shipped, what it reached, and which branches ordered because of it. What you get £40k to £48k Stock options 25 days holiday A laptop How to apply With your application, send us: 3 to 5 pieces of content you made yourself, ideally including one video you filmed and cut yourself (a phone is fine). Other examples: a social post or carousel, a campaign from idea to launch, a printed piece, a case study. For each one, a line on what you did and what it led to A few lines on how you use AI: which tools, for what, and one thing it let you ship How we will hire Send us 3 to 5 pieces you made and a few lines on how you work with AI A call with Jack, our CEO A short campaign task, then a call with our GTM Engineer to talk it through Present your idea to the team in person: the same idea, updated with what you'd change. 15 minutes, no new deck needed Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Social & Community Director, Esquire
description: <p><em>We are the UK's leading premium publisher, home to iconic and influential media brands including Esquire, Men's & Women's Health, ELLE, Good Housekeeping, Harper's Bazaar, Digital Spy, Cosmopolitan, Red and more. At Hearst UK, we don't just create content – we shape culture.</em></p> <p><em>Our workplace is driven by passion, shaped by authenticity and powered by creativity. We back bold ideas, act with an entrepreneurial mindset and continually evolve to meet the moment – while respecting the legacy that's brought us here. We believe in each other's potential and push boundaries together to create meaningful impact, both across the media landscape and in people's lives.</em></p> <p><em>We're proud of our heritage – but even more excited about making history.</em></p> <p><em>Hearst UK operates an in-office policy with flexible Fridays. Our office is based at <strong>House of Hearst, 30 Panton Street, St James's, London, SW1Y 4AJ</strong>, where teams collaborate in person and connect across brands and functions.</em></p> <p><strong>Salary – £50,000–£60,000</strong><br>Salary is dependent on experience and will be assessed in line with the candidate's skills, knowledge and relevant expertise.</p> <h2>The Role...</h2> <p>As Social & Community Director, you will own the success and growth of Esquire’s social platforms, with a particular focus on Instagram and TikTok. You will set the social strategy and editorial direction, translating Esquire’s wider editorial priorities into distinctive, high-performing, platform-native content that grows, engages and builds a lasting relationship with its audience.</p> <p>Working closely with editors, contributors and creative talent, you will bring Esquire’s editorial pillars to life across social, developing compelling formats and franchises that give audiences a reason to return. You will also play a key role in growing the commercial value of Esquire’s social channels, strengthening their place within the wider brand ecosystem.</p> <p>This is a highly visible editorial role. You will be a host and voice for Esquire, fronting social formats and video content and representing the brand with audiences, partners and at key cultural, brand and membership events.</p> <p>You will also help shape and grow Esquire’s new membership communities, hosting events, contributing to newsletters and working closely with the audience team to engage, nurture and build an active and connected community.</p> <h2>Main Duties...</h2> <ul> <li>Set Esquire’s social strategy across Instagram and TikTok, in line with the brand and wider editorial plans. Define clear audience priorities, content pillars and measures of success, adapting the approach as platforms, behaviours and audience habits evolve.</li> <li>Grow Esquire’s following and engagement in ways that build meaningful, lasting audience relationships. Use analytics, social listening and audience feedback to understand what is working, decide what to make next and continually improve performance.</li> <li>Develop distinctive social formats and franchises that give audiences a reason to return, including video fronted by Esquire’s editorial team. Host and present interviews, cultural coverage and original content, while helping other Esquire talent develop a natural and engaging voice on camera.</li> <li>Work closely with editors, writers, photographers, filmmakers, producers and contributors to commission and deliver distinctive, platform-native work. Set clear creative briefs and maintain high editorial and visual standards.</li> <li>Be hands-on in the filming and editing of social video content created by the editorial team, overseeing production and helping to develop regular, recognisable social franchises.</li> <li>Work closely with the commercial team to turn Esquire’s social reach, influence and expertise into valuable commercial opportunities. Develop partnership ideas that feel right for the brand and its audience, and contribute to pitches and presentations.</li> <li>Make Esquire’s social channels a valuable part of the wider brand ecosystem, strengthening the connections between social, editorial, partnerships, events and membership and increasing the commercial value of the channels.</li> <li>Work across editorial, digital and commercial teams to coordinate coverage, maximise major cultural and brand moments and ensure social is embedded within Esquire’s wider plans.</li> <li>Conceive, host and support events that bring Esquire’s audience together. Work with editorial and commercial colleagues to shape the right experiences, host or moderate conversations and extend their value through social coverage.</li> <li>Represent Esquire at selected partner, industry and audience events, acting as a highly visible ambassador for the brand and protecting the trust audiences place in Esquire by upholding its editorial and brand standards.</li> <li>Set direction and priorities for colleagues and contributors working across social. Coach on-camera talent, build a strong and reliable network of contributors and work with the hubbed Social Media Executive to support Facebook targets.</li> <li>Oversee social publishing, including captions, accessibility, permissions and rights. Manage time, production resources and delegated budgets against agreed priorities, escalating significant financial, legal, reputational or brand issues early.</li> </ul> <h2>What We Are Looking For...</h2> <h3>Essential</h3> <ul> <li>Significant proven experience setting and delivering social strategy, with a strong track record of growing audiences, increasing engagement and improving performance.</li> <li>Expert knowledge of Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, including how platform behaviour and audience habits evolve, with strong experience using analytics and insight to shape content and community strategy.</li> <li>Proven experience creating social content for luxury, lifestyle or media brands, with experience working with luxury brands on commercial activity.</li> <li>Strong editorial judgement and a natural instinct for turning culture, fashion, film, music, art and the wider cultural conversation into distinctive, engaging social content.</li> <li>Experience developing social-first formats and franchises, with the ability to identify what audiences want and turn ideas into high-performing content.</li> <li>The confidence and ability to lead work across multiple teams, set clear creative and editorial standards, influence senior stakeholders and help on-camera contributors develop their confidence and skills.</li> <li>Proven experience developing commercial partnership ideas and growing the commercial value of social channels, while protecting editorial independence, audience trust and clear disclosure.</li> <li>Experience directing social-first production and working closely with editorial, video and creative teams.</li> <li>Confidence and credibility as a presenter, with experience hosting interviews, video formats, live conversations or other audience-facing content.</li> <li>Excellent writing, communication and presentation skills, with strong judgement when handling sensitive editorial, audience or reputational issues.</li> </ul> <h3>Desirable</h3> <ul> <li>Filming and editing skills, including Adobe Premiere Pro.</li> </ul> <h2>Benefits</h2> <p>Your benefits at Hearst UK are more than just extras – they are tools to help you thrive in every part of life.</p> <h3>Hearst Exclusives – Only for You!</h3> <ul> <li>Get adventurous with Good Housekeeping Taste and Beauty Testing Panels – yes, you could be trying the next big thing in beauty, food and drink.</li> <li>Snag luxe beauty steals at our legendary office sample sales – score big on top brands without breaking the bank!</li> </ul> <h3>Inclusion, Health & Wellbeing – Feel Your Best</h3> <ul> <li>Stay healthy with Specsavers eye care, a company-funded Health Cash Plan and access to mental health support.</li> <li>Get active and stress-free with discounted gym memberships and the Cycle to Work scheme.</li> <li>Embrace flexibility with Location Flex and Holiday Exchange to take time when you need it.</li> <li>Take time to give back with a Charity Day and access wellbeing resources whenever you need them.</li> <li>Join one of our Hearst ERG groups.</li> </ul> <h3>Financial Wellness – Boost Your Budget</h3> <ul> <li>Plan ahead with a generous Workplace Pension, Income Protection, Life Assurance and Season Ticket Loan for easier commuting.</li> <li>Make smarter money moves using Salary Finance tools, Financial Wellbeing sessions and Home Tech benefits to spread costs.</li> <li>Treat yourself with major discounts across London plus everyday savings via the HAPI at Hearst app.</li> </ul> <h2>Inclusion & Belonging</h2> <p>Hearst UK is deeply committed to using our influential brands to reflect the world we want to live in – one that respects, protects, represents and uplifts the voices and opinions of all people. As a business, we recognise the significant benefits of creativity, collaboration and innovation that come with diverse teams. Not only is diversifying the voices in our organisation the right thing to do, but it also helps us create powerful and exciting content that can be enjoyed by many more people. This is why we're working to build a sense of true belonging within our business and foster a culture in which everyone feels heard.</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Public Policy & Affairs Principal
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>COMPANY OVERVIEW</strong></p> <p>KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.</p></div><p><strong>TEAM OVERVIEW</strong></p> <p>KKR’s Public Policy & Affairs (PPA) function is responsible for shaping and executing the firm’s global public policy, regulatory, and external engagement strategy. title: Principal Research Scientist

PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.</div></div><h3><strong>Note: </strong>We are currently title: Senior Research Scientist, Health Economic Modelling
description: <p> </p> <p>Do you consider yourself a self-starter with a real passion for projects involving <strong>innovative methods in health economics</strong> and evidence synthesis? Do you love collaborating, moving the ball forward, and rolling up your sleeves? Are you a <strong>health economist</strong> with a passion for <strong>R programming</strong>?</p> <p>If so – we want to talk to you!  We are growing and seeking a <strong>Senior Research Scientist</strong> with experience in <strong>building</strong> <strong>health economic models in R</strong> to join our Evidence Synthesis and Decision Modelling team. You will collaborate with a <strong>highly specialized team</strong> of health economists, statisticians and researchers in global, methodologically innovative projects for our pharma and biotech clients.</p> <p><strong>Why join us?</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Innovative Culture</strong>: Experience the excitement of a start-up within a well-funded, established global organization.</li> <li><strong>Passionate Team</strong>: Work with a team that has a real passion for Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR) and prides itself on being visionary leaders in the field.</li> <li><strong>Growth Opportunities</strong>: Be part of a growing team that values collaboration and making a real difference in healthcare.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About you:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Experienced Health Economist</strong>: You have a background in health economics, statistics or a related field, HEOR experience, and a solid understanding of the pharmaceutical industry and drug reimbursement processes. You are skilled in preparing written documentation and presenting results using Microsoft Word and PowerPoint.</li> <li><strong>Effective Communication</strong>: You can present progress and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, either internally or externally.</li> <li><strong>Project and Time Management</strong>: You ensure timely delivery of project components, can work effectively individually and as part of a diverse team and have excellent independent organizational and time management skills.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required Experience and Competencies:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Master’s degree in health economics or statistics, or a related discipline</li> <li>Minimum of 4 years of relevant professional experience, ideally in a consulting environment serving biotech, pharmaceutical or healthcare clients</li> <li>Proven R programming skills, experience with programming simulation-based cost-effectiveness models in R</li> <li>Understanding of and experience in the application of statistical methods in health economics, e.g., parametric survival regression model extrapolation, network meta-analyses, probabilistic sensitivity analyses</li> <li>Experience with data analysis and statistical methodologies in the context of HTA, JCA and or regulatory submission, e.g., survival analysis, indirect treatment title: Senior Manager, Paid Social
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>ABOUT QUINCE</strong></span></p> <p>Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.</p> <p>What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>OUR CULTURE</strong></span></p> <p>Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.</p> <ul> <li>We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.</li> <li>Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. </li> <li>Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. </li> </ul> <p>If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.</p></div><p data-renderer-start-pos="2290" data-local-id="6a0d0d38-3057-4834-9012-12f09f19e465"><strong data-renderer-mark="true"><span class="fabric-text-color-mark" data-renderer-mark="true" data-text-custom-color="#0747a6"><u data-renderer-mark="true">THE ROLE </u></span></strong></p> <p data-renderer-start-pos="2301" data-local-id="6d5afd27-5970-45c1-b675-f5df64663cbf"><span class="fabric-text-color-mark" data-renderer-mark="true" data-text-custom-color="#0747a6"><strong>Senior Manager, Paid Social</strong></span></p> <p data-renderer-start-pos="2320" data-local-id="f6597815-fb6f-48c2-a22a-55ab8b3f15f3"><span class="fabric-text-color-mark" data-renderer-mark="true" data-text-custom-color="#0747a6">We are seeking a <strong>Senior Manager, Paid Social</strong></span> <em data-renderer-mark="true"><span class="fabric-text-color-mark" data-renderer-mark="true" data-text-custom-color="#0747a6">to join our growing team. </span></em></p> <p>Paid social is one of the main ways Quince finds new customers, and this role sits at the centre of it. As Senior Manager, Growth Marketing (Paid Social), you will own strategy, execution and optimisation across Meta and other social platforms for a set of Quince departments, turning business goals into efficient media investment and steady, scalable growth.</p> <p>This is a hands-on, analytical role. You will manage significant media budgets against clear efficiency targets (ROAS, CAC and NC MTA ROAS), work out what is really driving performance, and work closely with creative, merchandising and analytics colleagues so that targeting and creative keep getting better. The role is critical to scaling our paid social acquisition engine.</p> <p data-renderer-start-pos="2663" data-local-id="e0c03b8d-8a8f-42ae-b3e9-26b5a2308ae6"><strong data-renderer-mark="true"><span across different attribution frameworks.</li> <li>Identify what drives incremental customer acquisition and revenue growth, and turn those findings into practical campaign and creative decisions.</li> <li>Build and maintain dashboards, reporting frameworks and performance analyses.</li> <li>Work with our analytics team to improve the accuracy of measurement and attribution.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Creative and testing collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work closely with the Creative, Studio and Production teams to shape creative that performs.</li> <li>Develop ways of working that title: Applied AI Engineering Manager, Startups | Core
description: About the Team The Applied AI Engineering team partners closely with customers to help them move from experimentation to production with OpenAI’s technologies. We act as trusted technical advisors, working across customer strategy, architecture, deployment, and adoption to help organizations realize meaningful impact from frontier AI. The Startups segment serves fast-moving, high-growth companies that are often building new products, workflows, and businesses directly on top of AI. These customers move quickly, operate with high ambiguity, and expect practical, creative, and technically rigorous partnership. About the Role We are looking for an Applied AI Engineering Manager, Startups to lead and scale the Startups Applied AI Engineering motion. This team helps high-growth startups move quickly from experimentation to production, unlock meaningful usage, and build durable technical partnerships with OpenAI. This leader will operate in a high-velocity customer segment where founders, CTOs, and technical teams expect speed, judgment, and hands-on problem-solving. They will balance team leadership, technical depth, customer prioritization, and cross-functional influence across Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and broader go-to-market teams. In this role, you will define how OpenAI supports startup customers at scale: identifying where deep technical engagement can unlock outsized impact, building repeatable deployment mechanisms, and ensuring the team can serve a broad and dynamic customer base without losing quality or strategic focus. In this role, you will: Craft and continuously refine the strategic vision and operating model for the Startups Applied AI Engineering team, aligning it with OpenAI’s broader company objectives and the evolving needs of high-growth startup customers. Lead, mentor, and grow a team of high-performing technical ICs supporting startup customers across AI-native, developer-led, and product-led companies. Help startups move from early experimentation to production usage by identifying technical blockers, advising on architecture, and driving practical paths to deployment. Partner closely with Sales to determine where technical engagement can accelerate adoption, production usage, and long-term account growth. Represent the technical voice of startup customers by synthesizing high-signal feedback, especially around developer experience, product gaps, deployment blockers, model performance, and emerging use cases. Translate recurring startup needs into repeatable playbooks, starter packs, reference architectures, internal tooling, and customer-facing assets that help the broader team move faster. Serve as a senior technical escalation point for priority startup customers, including founder-, CTO-, and technical executive-level conversations. Balance urgent customer needs with OpenAI’s broader product and platform priorities, especially when startups request niche features, bespoke support, or accelerated roadmap changes. Coach Applied AI Engineers on technical quality, customer judgment, prioritization, executive communication, and cross-functional partnership. Partner across Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and other GTM teams to improve how OpenAI supports startups from early adoption through scaled production usage. You might thrive in this role if you: Have proven experience founding, scaling, or operating within early-stage startups, ideally in technical leadership roles where you owned both product or customer outcomes and technical execution. Have a strong track record of building and leading technical, customer-facing teams in high-growth, ambiguous, or startup-heavy environments. Bring strong technical depth across APIs, platform products, AI/ML systems, developer workflows, and production deployment considerations. Have experience creating scalable operating models, not just managing one-off customer escalations. Are comfortable working directly with founders, CTOs, technical executives, and highly technical ICs. Demonstrate strong judgment about when to go deep for a strategic customer versus when to build repeatable mechanisms for the broader segment. Can translate complex technical and product considerations into clear decisions, practical guidance, and customer-facing recommendations. Operate with speed, iteration, and pragmatic customer impact without sacrificing quality, safety, or OpenAI’s long-term platform strategy. Are personally committed to fostering the safe and beneficial development of AI. Success will be measured by: A strong cadence of successful customer sprints and production-oriented technical engagements. Strong Product and Research feedback loops informed by startup customer needs and emerging use cases. Increased startup account usage, including tokens, requests, and production workloads. High-quality customer stories, founder and CTO satisfaction, and referenceable startup wins. Creation of repeatable startup deployment patterns, starter packs, templates, and reference architectures. A healthy, high-performing team with strong prioritization, clear operating mechanisms, and the ability to scale coverage across a high-demand segment. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. title: Senior CRM Executive - Lifecycle
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. About the team This position will be part of the central CRM & Ops team, composed of 18+ specialists, dedicated to driving and executing global strategic initiatives to grow and retain our New Customer base. Serving as the voice of the customer, the CRM & Ops team does this by enhancing personalised user experiences, activating best-in-class campaigns, and putting relevancy at the heart of everything. The Role As a Marketing Manager within the Lifecycle CRM & Ops team you are the voice of Deliveroo when speaking with our customers across the globe. You'll operate under a hybrid work model, spending a minimum of three days a week at our London HQ. Reporting into the Senior Marketing Manager on the New Customer squad, and working closely with stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Global CRM, Marketing Promotions, and Data Science, You'll be a technical, commercially minded CRM marketer who is hands-on in the tooling: building Lifecycle journeys, setting up experiments and audiences, and configuring promotions and in-app merchandising. You'll have end-to-end ownership of the New Customer Lifecycle, from journey design and build through to measurement and ROI. You'll also use personalisation and AI to make journeys more relevant. Your primary focus will be on creating customer-centric journeys that are highly relevant, using the right channels at the right time to deliver meaningful business impact, while working with local markets as you scale your initiatives internationally. What you'll be doing Collaborate with multiple stakeholders to support growing the new customer base by combining data-driven insights with CRM best practice to initiate and deliver programs internationally Build and configure multi-channel journeys (email, push, in-app), including audience logic, triggers, testing and QA Design and build multi-variant Lifecycle experiments Create promotions for new customer acquisition and retention, ensuring accurate setup, targeting and tracking Manage in-app merchandising placements, working with Product and Marketing Promotions Deliver personalisation at scale, and test where AI can improve content and efficiency Own operational delivery, optimisation, reporting of campaigns and weekly trading Proactively monitor and report on campaigns to stakeholders & propose/manage changes and optimisations where necessary Collaborate with the New Customer Lifecycle Manager and Marketing Promotions teams to develop the global CRM new customers lifecycle strategy Collaborate with stakeholders on key projects to create and implement test strategies that optimises performance of new & existing campaigns Be comfortable with data targeting, segmentation & analysis - pulling it, manipulating it and interpreting it, whilst using marketing technology to help achieve customer touchpoints faster and more efficiently than ever before Drive innovative ideas and solutions in response to business and customer needs Provide regular communication with stakeholders, such as the central marketing team, product and engineering teams and local markets, to ensure workloads & deadlines are managed efficiently (we love Slack channels for everything) Conduct post campaign reporting, pulling out the most interesting lessons and using these to guide your future ideas Requirements Bachelor's Degree (Marketing or Business preferred) or strong relevant experience A minimum of 3+ years CRM experience Can work in a fast-paced environment and prioritise workload Attention to detail and campaign deadlines are adhered to, maintaining high standards of accuracy Highly computer literate with: HTML familiarity (ability to understand where changes need to be made) Liquid logic Technical knowledge in CRM automation development Good communication skills and ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders groups Data visualisation tools & reporting experience (Looker preferred) CRM deployment experience (Braze or similar is a plus!) We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it. title: Senior Staff Product Engineer
description: About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Engineering team At hyperexponential, engineering is at the heart of our mission to transform the insurance industry. Our engineers build and scale, enabling insurers to model complex risks and make smarter pricing decisions at speed. By combining deep technical expertise with creativity, the team pushes the boundaries of what’s possible in insurance technology. Within engineering, our product teams are cross-functional, pairing frontend and backend engineers with designers and product managers. This enables end-to-end ownership of features, with engineers contributing across design, architecture, implementation, and testing. Collaboration is a core part of how we work, ensuring that every release is both technically sound and valuable to our users. How we work We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder , and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work. We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods , usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart. We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move. Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest. A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer. The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 5 , that looks like this. What you'll be doing Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion. Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced. Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve. Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting. Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you. Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating. What you'll need to have done Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered. Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve. Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps. Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to. Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce. Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity. Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them. At Level 5 we'll also look for Set technical direction on a hard problem other engineers built on, and been judged on whether you made them faster and safer rather than on the size of your team. Held a quality bar across other people's work without becoming the gate they wait on. Led cross-cutting or decoupling work that teams adopted because it was the best path, not because it was mandated. You’re unlikely to thrive here if You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach. You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges. You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Initial chat with our Talent team Lead Hirer Interview Live AI Skills Assessment Values Interview with the CPTO Meet the CEO Our commitment to Diversity hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. Next steps If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome. For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy. title: Sales Manager, UK - SMB/MM/Enterprise
description: About Dust Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026. Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 . The Role We’re hiring a hands-on sales leader for the UK. You’ll build, lead, and coach the regional Sales team, deliver against ARR and pipeline goals, and build a repeatable local growth engine. You'll act as the business lead for your market, with accountability for revenue. As a sales leader, you'll lead and coach the sales team, stay close to customers and deals, and build a repeatable sales approach that fits your market. As an orchestrator, you'll coordinate the local pipeline generation activities that feed your number, including marketing and pre-sales. You'll work closely with leaders across BDR, Growth, Field Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Solutions Engineering, Deployment, and Customer Success, and influence how they support your market's priorities. What you’ll do Own the region’s ARR plan, forecast, and qualified pipeline. Work with the CRO to set priorities, understand capacity needs, and support the team to deliver against the plan. Build and lead the regional Sales team. Hire, onboard, coach, and develop sellers, while staying hands-on in priority opportunities from prospecting and discovery through qualification, evaluation, negotiation, and close. Make clear, evidence-based recommendations to Product based on regional customer conversations, deal patterns, and market needs. Build and refine a repeatable regional sales approach using pipeline, win/loss learning, and customer outcomes. Drive the plan in partnership with field marketing to set priorities for events, campaigns, customer advocacy and community programs, and direct how field marketing resources are used to support your pipeline and ARR goals. Partner with the marketing leadership, who own field marketing standards, methods and team management, to make sure regional programs are well executed, measured and consistent with Dust's broader marketing approach Partner with BDR and Growth leaders to build a qualified pipeline through a deliberate mix of outbound and other locally effective channels. Set direction for how Partnerships can support regional priorities. Work with the Partnerships lead to identify opportunities for sourcing, co-selling, or delivery. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering, Deployment, Professional Services, and Customer Success to support credible evaluations, successful implementations, customer outcomes, and expansion. Represent regional customer needs internally and share market learning with the CRO and functional leaders, contributing to consistent GTM practices across Dust. Market-specific focus United Kingdom Build on early customer and partner traction. Use customer referrals, targeted events, and focused market experiments to build qualified pipeline and strengthen local customer proof. What we’re looking for A proven sales professional who has grown from individual contributor into people leadership, with 5+ years leading B2B software sales and coaching regional sales teams and a hands-on understanding of how to help reps succeed in-market. You've owned a market or segment revenue number end to end, not just a team's quota. You've built pipeline through functions you didn't manage, such as marketing, partners and pre-sales, and you've made real calls about where capacity and budget go, including between direct sales and partners Ability to lead by example in priority opportunities, from discovery through close. Experience building pipeline and customer relationships in a market where the brand or sales motion is still developing. A disciplined approach to forecasting and performance feedback, paired with high EQ and a genuinely supportive leadership style. An appetite for building, testing, and refining a market over multiple quarters while balancing near-term results with durable growth. What success looks like The region delivers against its ARR and pipeline goals while developing a repeatable sales approach suited to local customers. The team builds customer trust and referenceable outcomes, cross-functional support is focused on regional priorities, and market learning informs Dust’s broader GTM approach. Location We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together. We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect. That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call. Why Dust The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves. We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk. Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. Learn how we think and work. Our product constitution, a story about our mission Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human , Stanislas Polu , VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them. Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI , Gabriel Hubert , Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. title: (Senior) Marketing & Communications Manager, UK
description: Change.org is looking for a (Senior) Marketing & Communications Manager to lead our organisation and team in the UK as Market Lead and be the public face of Change.org in the country. Your job is to make the country notice. You will create big, viral campaigns, online and offline, that put the everyday people who start petitions on Change.org at the centre of the national conversation. You will lead a small, high-performing team, open doors through deep networks across UK politics, civil society, civic tech, newsrooms, broadcasters, and use AI to move faster than anyone else in the news cycle. We'd welcome ambitious and entrepreneurial Communications Manager level candidates with leadership presence, who are ready to step up into a team leadership role. Change.org is the world's largest petition platform, used by more than 100 million people every year to take part in civic life and democracy. At a time when dissatisfaction with democracy is at an all-time high, we are investing heavily in AI to build the most powerful tools in the world to give people a voice, while bringing people across the political spectrum together around shared solutions. What you will achieve Create awareness spikes . Regularly turn petitions from Change.org petition starters into national moments that people talk about, through viral campaigns that combine top-tier media, social media, video, creators and offline actions such as stunts, petition handovers and public events. Turn those moments into measurable growth for Change.org in the UK, such as new petition starters, signers and supporters. At a Senior Manager level, own the UK team's goals and report on how campaigns contribute to Change.org 's wider growth targets. Put petition starters in the spotlight. Find the strongest stories and the most credible, unexpected voices, and give them the visibility they need to win. Coach them on strategy, find the route to victory, and help them build the pressure that gets decision makers to act. Earn trust across the political spectrum . Make sure Change.org campaigns speak to people across the democratic political spectrum, and protect the trust in our brand as the team moves fast with AI. At a Senior Manager level, build balance checks, transparent reporting and training into how the team works, so every campaign protects our trusted, non-partisan brand. Mobilise your network . Use and grow high-trust relationships with senior editors, producers, journalists, politicians, decision makers, civil society, civic tech and creators to secure top-tier coverage and move decision makers. Show up in person at the events, meetings and petition deliveries where those relationships are built, many of them in London and Westminster. Be our voice. Act as Change.org 's external spokesperson in the UK on TV, radio, in print and on stage, representing a trusted, open platform for people across the democratic political spectrum, including in sensitive and crisis situations. Lead a high-performing team. Set clear goals, coach and develop people, give direct feedback, and build a culture of speed, ambition and ownership where people feel supported, trusted and able to do their best work, alongside a pace that matches the news cycle. Work closely with product, data and colleagues in other markets, and contribute to global campaigns and projects. At a Senior Manager level, set team objectives, coach and develop each person on the team, and lead or shape at least one cross-functional or global project that moves a wider business goal. Lead with AI, shape the product. Build AI and agentic workflows into how the team spots stories, plans campaigns, pitches media and reports results, so the team works faster and smarter. Work closely with Change.org ’s product team as the voice of UK user groups. Test new tools and features early, feed back what works and what doesn’t, and turn launches into moments in the UK, showing petition starters how new features can help them win. What you bring A track record of viral campaigns. You have created campaigns that broke through nationally and drove measurable spikes in public attention, online and offline. You think in moments, images and headlines, and you move from idea to execution in hours, not weeks. You use performance data and testing to decide which stories to back, how to pitch them and when to change course. Fast paced. You are skilled in fast and excellent execution with rapid pivots and changing contexts. An active network. You have active and trusted networks into UK politics (including key decision makers), civil society and civic tech, across the whole democratic political spectrum, including on the left, in the centre and on the right. You bring trusted relationships with UK journalists, editors and producers. You can use your contacts to place stories and move decision makers. Management. You have led and developed a team, or have mentored others and are ready to step into leading one. You care about the people you manage and know how to build a team that’s positive, ambitious and pulls together under pressure. You’re happy rolling up your sleeves alongside them. At Senior Manager level, you have hired, managed performance and navigated team conflict, and you adapt your style to get the best from each person. Leadership presence. You are confident, credible and calm under pressure. You are confident on camera and in front of senior stakeholders, with some spokesperson experience or the appetite to build it. AI-first, curious about civic tech. You use AI tools every day and have built or improved workflows and automations with them. You know where AI adds speed and quality and where human judgement matters most, and you bring your team along. You’re excited by new tools and how people use them. You’re comfortable testing features, spotting what users need, and giving product teams clear, practical feedback. Target experience 5-8+ years in digital campaigning, political campaigns and communications or public affairs, at a campaigning organisation, charity, political party or agency. 3+ years leading people, at Senior Manager level. We're also open to candidates at Manager level who have experience mentoring others and the ambition to lead a team. A proven track record of national campaigns in the UK that created significant public attention and media coverage. Experience as an organisation's spokesperson in national broadcast and / or print media. Hands-on experience using AI in communications or campaigning work. Interested? Great! Here's what you should know This is a full-time, remote role based in the United Kingdom. Deep networks into UK politics, civil society and civic tech are core to the role, as is regular, in-person presence at events, meetings and petition deliveries, many of which happen in London. We expect up to weekly travel into London and travel costs to London are not covered by Change.org . Our compensation philosophy is based on pay equity. All of our salaries are determined before we launch a role, based on a predetermined salary scale, the level on that scale and the cost of labour for that location. The annual salary for this role at Senior Manager level is £86,000 in the UK. We are also open to candidates at the Manager level and the annual salary in the UK is £75,500. These salaries are the same wherever in the UK you live. We recognise that people assess their qualifications differently, and you may not meet every requirement listed. If you believe you could be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply. Change.org is an open platform designed to serve people across the full range of viewpoints. Effectively supporting that mission requires teams with a wide variety of experiences, skills and perspectives, which we consider essential to our work. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span class="TextRun SCXW142035299 BCX0" lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW142035299 BCX0">Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL)</span></span><span data-contrast="none"> is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest </span><span data-contrast="none">health threats. </span><span data-contrast="none">Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We work toward a future where people live</span> <span data-contrast="none">longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p></div><p><span class="EOP SCXW70040856 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}">Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) works with governments and partners to strengthen and transform primary health care (PHC) to improve health and save lives. Our approach focuses on making PHC more prioritized, proactive and accountable for outcomes, and strengthening how care is organized, delivered, financed and measured. Drawing on expertise across RTSL's portfolio, we bring together solutions in health system resilience and epidemic readiness, digital health and data-driven decision-making, performance measurement and improvement, and sustainable health financing. We apply these capabilities to address priority health challenges, including cardiovascular health, maternal survival and sexual and reproductive health, while strengthening health systems to deliver more equitable, effective and resilient care.  </span></p> <h3><strong><span class="EOP SCXW70040856 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}">Position Purpose</span></strong></h3> <p>The Director, Maternal & Reproductive Health will provide strategic and technical leadership for RTSL's portfolio to reduce preventable maternal deaths and improve sexual and reproductive health outcomes. The role will lead the development and implementation of a multi-country program that strengthens government capabilities to identify and address barriers to quality care, translate data into action, and deliver measurable improvements in health outcomes.</p> <p>The Director will have overall accountability for the strategy, resources, quality, performance, and results of the maternal survival and reproductive health portfolio, leading a multidisciplinary team and working closely with governments, technical partners, and colleagues across RTSL to design, implement and scale evidence-informed approaches. The role requires deep expertise in sexual, reproductive and maternal health, strong program leadership, and the ability to translate technical evidence into practical, sustainable health system improvements.</p> <p><span data-contrast="auto"><strong>Work Location: </strong>100% Remote with travel as stated. </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto"><strong>Duration:</strong> Full-time employment for a fixed term of 24 months.</span></p> <h3><strong><span class="EOP SCXW70040856 BCX0" data-ccp-props="{}">Core Duties and Responsibilities</span></strong></h3> <h4><strong>Strategic</strong> <strong>Leadership</strong> <strong>and Portfolio Management</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Set the strategic direction, priorities and implementation approach for RTSL's maternal survival and reproductive health portfolio, exercising delegated authority to make program investment, resource allocation, and partnership decisions within approved organizational parameters and in alignment with country priorities.</li> <li>Oversee a multi-country portfolio, with accountability for program planning, budget development and management, resource allocation, performance and delivery against strategic objectives.</li> <li>Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team, establishing clear responsibilities and performance expectations, overseeing staffing and talent development, addressing performance and capacity gaps, and building the capabilities needed for sustained program delivery.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Technical Leadership and Program Development</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Provide expert technical leadership across maternal survival and sexual and reproductive health, including maternal death surveillance and response, quality maternal care, family planning, and adolescent pregnancy prevention.</li> <li>Lead the development and adaptation of evidence-informed approaches that connect data-driven learning with targeted improvements in clinical care, service delivery and wider health system capabilities.</li> <li>Guide the design and implementation of country programs, identifying opportunities to strengthen government leadership, institutional capabilities and sustainable approaches to improving health outcomes.</li> <li>Drive innovation and collaboration across RTSL's technical teams, drawing on expertise in PHC delivery, digital health, measurement and financing to address priority health system bottlenecks.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Country Engagement and Strategic Partnerships</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Lead senior-level engagement with with donors, multilateral agencies, technical institutions and implementing partners, identifying opportunities for collaboration, investment and program expansion, and representing RTSL in high-level technical and policy discussions.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Performance, Learning and Accountability</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Maintain overall accountability for portfolio performance and results, establishing clear performance expectations and monitoring mechanisms, and using evidence and implementation learning to inform strategic decisions, address delivery challenges, and adapt approaches.</li> <li>Oversee the generation, synthesis and dissemination of evidence and practical learning to inform policy, program improvement and scale-up across countries.</li> </ul> related field.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Experience</strong></h4> <ul> <li>At least 15 years of relevant global health experience, including substantial technical and leadership experience in sexual, reproductive and maternal health in low- and middle-income countries.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience developing and leading complex, multi-country programs, including strategic planning, budget oversight and accountability for results.</li> <li>Extensive experience engaging senior government officials, donors and international partners, with the ability to build relationships and influence strategic decisions.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Skills & Abilities</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Recognized technical expertise in maternal survival and reproductive health, with a strong understanding of evidence-based interventions, health service delivery and health system strengthening.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead and develop multidisciplinary teams and manage programs across different countries and organizational functions.</li> <li>Strong understanding of data-driven program improvement, implementation challenges and approaches to translating evidence into sustainable Experience designing production systems with complex multi-tenancy, data isolation or data lifecycle requirements. Strong experience integrating with third-party APIs and designing for rate limits, partial failures, retries and reconciliation. A strong understanding of reliability, observability, security and operational ownership. Experience making architectural trade-offs and communicating technical decisions clearly to engineering teams and stakeholders. A track record of mentoring engineers and raising engineering standards. The ability and desire to remain hands-on while providing technical direction to a team. Desirable Production experience with Python alongside Node.js. Experience with identity and access management technologies such as Auth0, AWS Cognito or similar. Strong understanding of OAuth 2.0 and authentication/authorisation patterns. Experience building software within financial services or another regulated environment. At the same time, you’ll create leverage by helping the engineers around you make better decisions and take greater ownership. You’ll be comfortable asking questions before reaching for a solution, thinking through failure modes as carefully as the happy path, and balancing architectural quality with the realities of delivering software in a fast-growing business.
